_doc: The 2D cards after the song (brief, 'Bookends, fact card and cuts'), read by scripts/overlay_cues.py. Facts render only when facts_checked is true, set after the source check is logged (docs/fact_check_2026-10-26.md). Card lines are the check's proposed wording: cards 1 and 2 of its list merged back into the brief's first fact; the VulnCheck snapshot replaced by Anthropic's dashboard figures with their date. End-card values in {braces} are filled by overlay_cues.py: the intervention count from log/human_interventions.md, the repo URL from config/release.json.

facts.text: Anthropic's restricted model, Claude Mythos Preview, found a 27-year-old bug in OpenBSD, among thousands of high-severity vulnerabilities it says it found.
Access went to a limited group of partners through Project Glasswing, with up to $100M in usage credits.
By October 2, 2026, Anthropic counted 29,439 candidate findings: 6,157 disclosed, 516 patched.
Anthropic says the limit is now how fast bugs can be verified, disclosed and patched.
Mozilla found and fixed 271 vulnerabilities in a single Firefox release while testing the model.
Node.js maintainers report “an incredible amount of AI slop” in vulnerability reports.
In August 2026, researchers using OpenAI and Google models found PHP2Shell, flaws in the language behind about 70% of websites whose server-side language is known.
When the fix shipped on October 21, government sites from Britain to Japan went offline while operators patched.
Anthropic's stated reason for withholding: without safeguards, such models would make exploiting flawed software cheaper for almost anyone.
Critics call the arrangement “a private club.”
facts.source: SecurityPal, citing Georgia Tech's Internet Governance Project

facts.text: Mythos Preview's successor is the same underlying model as Claude Fable, which Anthropic sells publicly with added safeguards.
